data.name: Cesare
data.gender_notes: Cesare is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin name Caesar, meaning 'long-suffering' or 'loving'. This name was borne by several early Christian saints, including St. Ceasarius of Arles and St. Cesarius of Liguria. The name Cesare carries the meaning “Long-suffering, loving” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Cesare usually hope their child will grow to embody long-suffering, loving and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Cesare belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Long-suffering, loving.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Cesare total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_greek.name: Κεζαρε
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Κεζαρε σημαίνει μακρύς ή βασιλιάς
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κεζαρε είναι η ελληνική εκδοχή του λατινικού ονόματος Καισαρ, που σημαίνει μακρύς ή βασιλιάς. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, ο όρος Καισαρ αναφέρεται συχνά στον Ρωμαϊκό Αυτοκράτορα, συμβολίζοντας την κοσμική εξουσία. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα Κεζαρε έχει συσχετιστεί με την πνευματική και εγκόσμια ηγεσία.

data.cultural_impact: The name Cesare has its roots in the ancient Roman civilization and was adopted as a given name amongst the Early Christians in Europe. It has been a common name in various regions, including Italy and Spain, and is still used in these countries today.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Cesare holds significant spiritual meaning for Christians as it was borne by several saints who demonstrated remarkable patience and love towards others. The name inspires a sense of hope, endurance, and forgiveness, urging us to be more compassionate towards one another like the early Christian saints bearing this name. Ultimately, the name Cesare is a reminder of the importance of love and patience in our lives as we strive to grow in the Christian faith.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Cesare may be derived from the Latin word "caesar," meaning "he who cuts," symbolizing strength, leadership, and decisive action. In Christian tradition, St. Cesarius of Arles embodied these qualities, leading his people with courage and compassion.

historical_references.reference: Cesare Borgia, a son of Pope Alexander VI, was born in 1475 and became a cardinal in 1492. He is infamous for his ruthless power struggles and political maneuverings during the Italian Wars.
Cesare della Rovere, born in 1492, became Duke of Ferrara in 1505. He was a patron of the arts, and his court became a center for humanist scholars and artists.
